maya: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a sharp regress for the 'legal_short' prompt set, lots of low-quality hallucinations starting 2103345600 UTC, spike across multiple quantized model variants. sample: 'The plaintiff confirmed the case was dismissed because of the judge's cat.'
liam: ugh. Is that coming from a single shard or widespread?
jess: eval-bot posted the rollup earlier, looks like 42 failures across 6 workers, 3 timeouts. link: https://s3.redwood/ci/nightly/2103345600/report.json :eyes:
eval-bot: nightly-eval: model=gptx-q4_0, prompts=legal_short, failures=42, timeouts=3, avg_latency=312ms
tom: I pulled a failing sample and repro'd locally with quantized binary. non-deterministic: two runs with same seed produced different truncations and once hung waiting on tokenizer step. logs attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-04 02:34:12] tokeniser: input bytes length=278, normalized=NFC
[2026-03-04 02:34:12] spm::Encode -> 87 tokens
[2026-03-04 02:34:13] kv-cache: waiting for lock (2000ms)
[2026-03-04 02:34:15] runtime: sample loop exceeded timebox
```
maya: Wait — normalized=NFC? Our harness normalizer should be using NFKC for compatibility with the tokenizer preprocessor. when did this change land?
jess: there's a tiny change in eval-harness 0.9.7 that toggled unicode normalizer to default Python str.normalize('NFC') in attempt to be "faster". iirc tokenizer (sentencepiece) was trained on NFKC.
liam: if tokenization differs then logits alignment + kv cache keys could diverge, causing long waits or cache mismatches -> timeouts. makes sense.
tom: quick check: i ran this small script on the failing input, NFC vs NFKC produced different token counts:
```
import unicodedata
from sentencepiece import SentencePieceProcessor
s='Plaintiff–defendant
(see § 5)'
print(unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s))
print(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s))
sp=SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='spm.model')
print(len(sp.encode(unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s))))
print(len(sp.encode(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s))))
```
jess: interesting — NFKC collapses the en-dash + ligatures into plain chars; that matches training. that could shift token offsets and break cache keys.
maya: has anyone repro'd the nondeterministic hangs on non-quantized (fp16) builds? if yes then it's harness-only, if not then it's quantization-induced fragility.
tom: fp16 run didn't hang, produced consistent tokens with NFKC. quantized runner uses a fast path that assumes stable tokenization + exact shape matching; mismatches cause the batching/kvcache code to spin waiting for expected keys.
liam: mitigation: pin eval-harness to normalize('NFKC') and add a unit test comparing token counts across normalization modes for all prompt sets. also add a safety timeout in kvcache wait with clearer metrics.
maya: agreed. can someone open a PR? mark as P0 for nightly stability. also tag eng-runtime because this exposed a brittle assumption in the fast-path. :bangbang:
jess: opening PR with tests and revert to NFKC, will include reproducer and CI case for quantized runner. PR draft in 10m.
eval-bot: update: ticket created ENGML-4621 (eval-harness: force NFKC normalizer + kvcache guardrail).
